objective: Continuation authorized by the owner on 2026-10-31 ('Yes, let's continue.'), taking the recommendation of PLAIN-COUNT-20261031-001: decide whether counting 2-colourings is #P-hard on plain cubic Pfaffian braces, or whether plain trisum braces hide another tractable structure. Scoping before activation (not evidence): (i) all 2500 plain ladder steps (a junction of two plain pages followed by a rung, no caps) are nonsingular; one step generates a 4-dimensional commutative algebra, two generic steps the full 8-dimensional parity-block algebra; (ii) running wire B the other way makes a crossing site exactly (NW)^k, so the exact crossing is the identity, the k = 0 term; (iii) with two plain cube pages, #col(K3,3) = 6 is recovered from instances with 1, 3, 5, 7 junctions (20 to 104 vertices), each plain and certified Pfaffian, braces where tested; (iv) weaving a source with a 2-edge cut into a truncated-octahedron frame gives cyclically 4-edge-connected planar hosts and certified Pfaffian plain instances (4 placements, 638 to 1100 vertices). Questions: (A) prove that ladders of plain cube junctions interpolate to an exact crossing inside braces, with the lattice condition, and recover K3,3 from plain Pfaffian braces; (B) prove that counting on plain Pfaffian braces is #P-hard, by weaving a hard source into a planar brace frame (cyclic 4-edge-connectivity of the woven host, the cube junction lemma, Hall's condition for braces). No time constraints.
status: Complete: a plain crossing inside braces (ladders of plain cube junctions, (NW)^k with characteristic polynomial (x^2 - 19x - 1)(x^2 + 7x + 13)) and counting on plain Pfaffian braces is #P-hard (weaving into prism frames; bond, weaving and cube junction lemmas; Hall).
